q8.answer: Each customer has one counter in a single shared Redis, keyed rl:{customerId}:{windowNumber} where the window number is the minute from Redis TIME. Old counts are removed by a 120 s TTL on each key, so they expire on their own.

q9.answer: The budget resets at each fixed one-minute wall-clock boundary. A new window number gives a new key that starts at zero. There is no sliding window or gradual refill.

q10.answer: Each check is one atomic Lua script in Redis. Redis runs scripts one at a time, so the check and increment cannot interleave. Only one instance sees the count below the limit for the last slot, and the other gets denied.

q11.answer: The Lua script computes Retry-After as the whole seconds until the next minute window starts, rounded up, between 1 and 60. It uses Redis TIME, and the gateway puts it in the 429 header.

q12.answer: No, the gateway does not retry the store and has no local fallback counter. It emits ratelimit_store_unavailable, forwards the request, and adds no X-RateLimit-* headers, so the client gets the plain backend response with no rate-limit information.
